Evidence recorded from a sidecar running in an Intel TDX confidential VM. Public material only; no keys or secrets.

quote-boot.hex          the boot quote exactly as /attest served it (hex of the raw TDX v4 quote)
attest-boot.json        GET /attest (boot document)
attest-fresh.json       GET /attest?nonce=<nonce> ({ nonce, response })
receipt.json            a receipt the sidecar signed for one chat completion
sidecar-cert.crt        the certificate the sidecar presented
router-attestation.json GET /api/v1/attestation/:providerId as the router answered after verifying this quote, from a
                        local run of the router's own code

Edits made before committing:
  * the platform event log is removed from both /attest documents (it names the deployment);
  * the deployment host name in the certificate's subjectAltName is replaced by a same-length placeholder. That
    breaks the certificate's own self-signature, which no check here uses: the certificate is pinned, and what is
    checked is its attestation name and its public key;
  * the provider id in router-attestation.json is renamed.

The quote's Intel signature and certificate chain are untouched but are not verified by the SDK: the router does that.
